caption: United States v. Lewis
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
justification: PAGE CANDIDATE. Binding Sixth Circuit digital-consent-scope decision missing from content/cases. It limits consent to an on-site preview of a laptop/phone and rejects later seizure/forensic searches absent a valid warrant or other independent justification; useful for the consent-search digital-device gap already flagged in the node page.

caption: United States v. Kolsuz
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
justification: PAGE CANDIDATE. Binding Fourth Circuit and first-impression post-Riley border-device split marker missing from content/cases. It treats an off-site month-long Cellebrite-type phone examination as a nonroutine border search requiring individualized suspicion, filling the Fourth Circuit reasonable-suspicion side of the split.

caption: United States v. Aigbekaen
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
justification: PAGE CANDIDATE. Binding Fourth Circuit border-device narrowing case missing from content/cases. It adds the border-nexus limit: when a device search is intrusive enough to require individualized suspicion, the suspicion must relate to the border-search exception's sovereign purposes, not only ordinary domestic crime investigation.

caption: Alasaad v. Mayorkas
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
justification: PAGE CANDIDATE. Binding First Circuit border-device split marker missing from content/cases. The opinion, captioned Alasaad v. Wolf on Justia with Mayorkas substituted, holds no warrant or probable cause is required for advanced border device searches and rejects the Ninth Circuit-style limitation to digital contraband only.

caption: United States v. Perez
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
justification: PAGE CANDIDATE. Binding First Circuit SITA split marker missing from content/cases. It declines to extend Gant's reaching-distance limit to a carried backpack separated from an arrestee at search time, preserving Eatherton and expressly contrasting the Third, Fourth, Ninth, and Tenth Circuit approach.

caption: United States v. Eatherton
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
justification: MENTION ONLY. Older First Circuit antecedent preserved by Perez for carried containers incident to arrest. Real and important for First Circuit doctrine, but Perez is the stronger modern page candidate because it is the live split marker and updates Eatherton after Chadwick, Gant, and Riley.

caption: United States v. Knapp
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
justification: MENTION ONLY. Same-side SITA split marker cited in Perez for applying Gant/Chimel to a purse or carried container outside the automobile context. The corpus already has United States v. Howard Davis for the yes-extend side and Perez is the stronger missing opposing-side candidate.

caption: United States v. Cook
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
justification: MENTION ONLY. Same-side SITA split marker cited in Perez for applying Gant outside vehicle searches to a backpack. Useful for circuit naming, but not elevated because the yes-extend side is already represented in-corpus by Davis and the missing no-extend side is Perez.

caption: United States v. Shakir
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
justification: MENTION ONLY. Same-side SITA split marker cited in Perez for the reasonable-possibility-of-access test for a bag at arrest. Kept as a circuit-name marker rather than a page candidate because Davis plus Perez cover the actionable split directions.

caption: United States v. Vergara
court: U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit
justification: MENTION ONLY. Border-device no-warrant/probable-cause marker cited by Alasaad. Not elevated because the corpus already has United States v. Touset for the stronger Eleventh Circuit no-suspicion side of the forensic-device split.
